evidence: All survivors test "p1 + p2 > T" and then totals: "if total_p1 > T", "if sum1 > T", or default to "LOAD 2". They rely on the promise that one of these cases must apply.
affordance_in_statement: For every input in this problem, it is guaranteed that the deadline cannot be met... Exactly one of the following structural bottlenecks is guaranteed to apply for every input.
removal_suggestion: Do not promise that impossibility is exhausted by an isolated-job sum or a single-appliance load. Present the deadline as impossible while requiring the certificate to account for precedence interactions and the complete two-appliance schedule, with the JOB/LOAD text defining those checks indirectly rather than exposing the two simple inequalities.

common_affordance: The explicit promise that every impossible instance has exactly one of two simple certificates: p1+p2>T for some job, or a phase total exceeding T.
recommended_edit: Replace the explicit exhaustive-bottleneck guarantee and its direct descriptions with instances where deadline impossibility may arise from two-appliance precedence/order interactions, and define JOB/LOAD certificate validity in terms of the complete schedule-dependent obstruction rather than the isolated sum and aggregate-load tests.
